The geologic relationships between East and West Antarctica and the other southern continents are still not well understood. The geophysical work of RISP, Dry Valley Drilling Project (DVDP), and Eltanin, and the coring work done by Deep Sea Drilling Project (DSDP), DVDP, and RISP, will provide the kinds of information that are required to make intelligent reconstructions of the past geologic, volcanic, tectonic, and glacial history of the Ross Sea Embayment.
Meteorological Investigations
The deposition of chemical compounds from the Antarctic atmosphere occurs when precipitation scavenges the atmospheric aerosol particles to the surface. In Antarctic latitudes, two major precipitation-forming mechanisms, vapor diffusion and accretion, determine the rate of aerosol removal. These two mechanisms operate at markedly different rates and efficiencies in time and space. Preliminary observations made in Antarctica during the austral summer 1971-72 indicated that the relative importance of these two mechanisms varies significantly with distance from the ocean; the accretional component decreased with increasing distance from the ocean.
